findings.quote: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
findings.why: This verse is quoted as part of the flow of Psalm 23, but it is actually from John 10:11, not Psalm 23.

findings.quote: He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.
findings.why: This verse is inserted into the walking of Psalm 23, but it is actually from Isaiah 40:11, not Psalm 23.

narrative_value: The script is a deeply reflective, pastoral, and well-structured night prayer and meditation centered primarily on Psalm 23 and other comforting passages. It avoids manipulative fear-bait, false prophecies, and financial guarantees. While two verses from other books of the Bible are seamlessly woven into the reading of Psalm 23 without explicitly stating the book change, the overall narrative and teaching value is high, acting as a genuine devotional rather than mass-produced template filler.
